newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-NO ESCAPE FOR FRENCH AS CHANG ROLLS ON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NO ESCAPE FOR FRENCH AS CHANG ROLLS ON.

text.p: World number two Michael Chang continued his one-man assault on French tennis on Saturday by moving into the fourth round at Roland Garros at the expense of injured local hope Stephane Simian.

Chang, a favourite over the years at Roland Garros, is beginning to wear out his welcome with the Parisian crowd after collecting his third French scalp in as many matches when the unheralded Simian, ranked 135 in the world, retired with a groin strain in the second set with the American leading 6-1 5-2.
Chang, who arrived in Paris struggling to find the form that saw him win the 1989 title, appears to have found it after dropping just one set on his march into the final 16.

Simian, who before this week had never advanced past the first round of the French Open in four attempts, knew he was in for a difficult day early in the first set, treating his groin with ice at each changeover.
The Frenchman was finally forced to retire after aggravating the injury when attempting to chase down a Chang drop volley.
South African 13th seed Wayne Ferreira was another casualty, withdrawing with an ankle injury before his third round encounter with Petr Korda of the Czech Republic.

Chang, the top remaining seed after the exit of number one Pete Sampras on Friday, will face a much tougher test in his next match when he meets two-time champion Sergi Bruguera of Spain, who also appears to have rediscovered his winning form.

Monica Seles, winner of three consecutive French titles from 1990 to 1992, barely had to work harder than Chang to book her place in the fourth round as she crushed France's Nathalie Tauziat 6-0 6-1 in just 51 minutes in front of a quiet centre court crowd.

Two other former champions, Bruguera and Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, who gave Spain a sweep of the singles crowns in 1994, also sailed smoothly into the next round by sinking the last two remaining Belgium hopes.
Bruguera, the 16th seed, crushed Dick Norman 6-3 6-1 6-3 while sixth seed Sanchez Vicario moved closer to a fourth consecutive final appearance when she brushed aside Dominique Van Roost 6-0 6-3.
In her three matches Sanchez Vicario has yet to lose a set and has dropped just 10 games, spending less than an hour on court each time.
